recognize_zh: 周邊血中有標靶紅血球，並見數個含有棱角狀、指套或船形結晶的紅血球（SC crystal），部分細胞有直線折痕，偶見卵圓形紅血球，符合血紅素SC病。
features: Several red cells with angular, dense intraerythrocytic crystals or blunt, finger-like projections (SC cells)
Folded red cells with straight crease lines and dense angular cells
Target cells and cells with irregular central hemoglobin distribution
Occasional ovalocytes and a crenated (echinocytic) cell
No classic elongated sickle cells in the field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows scattered target cells together with red cells containing dense, angular hemoglobin crystals and folded cells with straight crease lines. Occasional ovalocytes and a crenated cell are noted. Typical elongated sickle cells are not seen in this field. Findings are consistent with hemoglobin SC disease; confirmation by hemoglobin HPLC or electrophoresis is recommended.

ddx.vs: HbC crystals are hexagonal or rod-shaped 'bar of gold' crystals within otherwise empty cells, whereas SC crystals are blunt, finger-like or glove-shaped, and HPLC distinguishes by the absence of HbS.
HbSS has abundant thin crescent-shaped sickle cells rather than dense angular crystal-containing cells and target cells.

ddx.dx: Red cell overlap or drying artifact
ddx.vs: Artifactual folds are seen in thick areas and lack dense hemoglobin concentrated in crystal-like shapes.
